default.intent: Present a deterministic Atlas component or composition fixture for visual-quality and robustness review without simulating a complete domain application.
intentional_traits: A fixture may place several variants, states, or roles side by side for comparison.
Text and data are deterministic demonstration content.
Native chrome consistent with the Slint renderer may remain visible.
invariants: No content may be clipped, overlap, or become unreadable.
Alignment, spacing, and hierarchy must follow a shared system.
Visible states must remain identifiable with credible contrast.
Whitespace must appear intentional or support a readable structure.
exclusions: Do not criticize a demonstration fixture for lacking rich domain data.
Do not report a consistent native scrollbar as an artifact.
Do not turn a personal density, radius, or color preference into a defect.

data.intent: Demonstrate Atlas data presentation: desktop tables, compact adaptation, loading, empty and error states, and controlled selection and expansion.
intentional_traits: The table and alternate states deliberately appear in one fixture.
Rows may simultaneously be selected, expanded, and disabled.
A narrow viewport may turn rows into cards instead of preserving columns.
invariants: Headers, cells, and actions must preserve readable axes in table mode.
Compact mode must not create horizontal overflow or clip essential content.
Selection, expansion, and disabled states must not rely on color alone.
Skeleton, empty, and error states must retain coherent geometry and hierarchy.
exclusions: Multiple row states shown together are intentional.
Responsive cards are not a loss of structure.
The deliberately truncated pull-request fixture demonstrates its tooltip contract.

components.intent: Present foundational Atlas components in controlled states to verify their consistency, hierarchy, and catalog composition.
intentional_traits: Variants and states of one component deliberately appear together.
Controls do not form a complete domain form.
Loading, disabled, invalid, and focus states may be forced for visual evidence.
invariants: Components in one family must share geometry, typography, and alignment.
Primary, secondary, danger, loading, and disabled actions must remain distinct.
Field labels, values, help, and errors must remain readable and associated.
No component may overflow, overlap, or touch a section boundary.
exclusions: Incompatible real-application states are juxtaposed intentionally.
The absence of a domain workflow is not a defect.
Different emphasis between variants is expected when it expresses role.

foundations.intent: Document Atlas foundations by comparing themes, semantic colors, three densities, and interactive states on one board.
intentional_traits: Dark and light themes deliberately appear together with different visual mass.
Compact, normal, and comfortable density rows appear simultaneously.
Interactive states are grouped on a demonstration surface.
invariants: Theme cards must retain identical geometry.
Density rows must differ in height while preserving alignment and padding.
Every semantic color must use readable content color.
No panel or control may touch or cross its boundary.
exclusions: The brightness of the light-theme card is not itself a defect.
Showing three densities together is not inconsistent.
A geometrically consistent native scrollbar is not an artifact.

navigation.intent: Demonstrate Atlas navigation and overlay components, selected states, focus, and layered surfaces.
intentional_traits: Menus, tooltips, tabs, or modals may be held open for capture.
Several navigation states may be juxtaposed.
Focus rings may be forced to make keyboard paths observable.
invariants: The active layer must be identifiable without hiding essential content.
Selected, active, disabled, and focused items must remain distinct.
Overlays must remain in the viewport and preserve padding, borders, and hierarchy.
Labels and shortcuts must not overlap or truncate without explicit intent.
exclusions: A permanently open fixture overlay is not a behavioral defect.
Forced focus does not imply multiple simultaneous native focus targets.
Intentional overlay layering is not accidental overlap.

wave.intent: Present complementary Atlas metrics, selection, progress, range, pagination, and key/value components as a coherent catalog composition.
intentional_traits: Functionally different components deliberately share one board.
Values, percentages, and statuses are deterministic demonstration data.
Semantic tones deliberately vary across components.
invariants: Components must share grid, radius, typography, labels, and vertical rhythm.
Primary values must dominate metadata and labels.
Controls must remain readable, contained, and aligned.
Semantic roles must retain credible contrast and hierarchy.
exclusions: Functional variety is not design-system inconsistency.
Status color differences are intentional.
The select control is offset beneath its label intentionally.

final.intent: Present the final Atlas application component set: alerts, workflow banner, notices, stepper, sparkline, contained drawer, and error page.
intentional_traits: Several feedback and navigation surfaces are visible simultaneously.
The drawer is contained in its demonstration cell rather than covering the viewport.
Success, warning, and error states use different emphasis intentionally.
invariants: Actions, titles, and messages must remain readable without overlap.
Panels in one row must preserve coherent axes, heights, and spacing.
The hierarchy between global feedback, progress, and recovery must be immediate.
Visualizations and contained overlays must stay within their cells.
exclusions: Simultaneous feedback levels are specific to the fixture.
Do not assess the contained drawer as a full-viewport application drawer.
The capture does not require real navigation.

editorial.intent: Demonstrate Atlas editorial foundations: semantic headings, paragraphs, code, quotation, divider, and reading measure.
intentional_traits: The content is an editorial fixture rather than a complete article.
The board may pair an article with the typographic scale.
Code blocks intentionally use monospace typography and distinct density.
invariants: H1, H2, body, lead, quotation, and metadata hierarchy must be clear.
Reading measure and vertical rhythm must remain regular.
Text must not clip, overlap, or become unreadable at declared viewports.
Editorial surfaces must share grid, radius, contrast, and typography tokens.
exclusions: Brief demonstration content is not a lack of domain richness.
Different prose and code densities are intentional.
Missing documentation interactions are not a defect on this board.

icons.intent: Present the Atlas icon registry and semantic roles in a deterministic grid.
intentional_traits: Glyphs are deliberately restrained, monochrome, and smaller than their cells.
Several functional roles and semantic tones are juxtaposed as a catalog.
Technical labels identify symbols and remain secondary.
invariants: Every icon must be crisp, centered, and identifiable at its declared size.
Cells must share dimensions, padding, axes, and rhythm.
Icons and labels must not overlap or leave their cells.
Semantic tones must remain readable in dark and light themes.
exclusions: Whitespace around a glyph is intentional breathing and hit area.
Simple geometry is not missing detail.
The catalog grid need not fill the viewport vertically.

responsive.intent: Demonstrate Atlas responsive primitives at contractual viewports: stack, cluster, sidebar, switcher, and automatic grid.
intentional_traits: Components are abstract layout diagrams rather than finished domain cards.
Badges and labels deliberately describe the active responsive mode.
At 360 px compositions may become vertical; at 720 px some retain two columns.
invariants: Nothing may overflow horizontally or be clipped.
Direction changes must preserve order, alignment, and tokenized spacing.
Touch targets and labels must remain usable at 360 px.
The viewport must unambiguously show the declared breakpoint behavior.
exclusions: The schematic appearance is intentional.
A page taller than the viewport may require native scrolling.
A narrow native ScrollView track is not a leaking border.

rich-content.intent: Present Atlas admonitions, links, tables, figures, and documentation blocks in a responsive native composition.
intentional_traits: Several documentation families deliberately share one catalog page.
Links and actions are host-controlled and do not navigate during capture.
Media and terminal content use deterministic placeholders.
invariants: Semantic blocks must retain clear hierarchy and readable contrast.
Tables, figures, and code must stay within their responsive bounds.
Interactive intentions must remain discoverable without appearing executed.
Long content must wrap or truncate according to an explicit contract.
exclusions: Inactive fixture links are not broken navigation.
Placeholder media is not missing production content.
Juxtaposing documentation families is intentional.

media-states.intent: Compare deterministic loading, ready, empty, and error states for documentation media.
intentional_traits: All media states appear together for comparison.
Media sources and errors are deterministic fixtures.
No real network loading occurs.
invariants: Every state must remain identifiable beyond color alone.
Media stages must share coherent geometry and alignment.
Messages and recovery actions must remain readable and contained.
Loading must respect the declared motion preference.
exclusions: Simultaneous media states are intentional.
Fixture placeholders are not missing assets.
The capture does not prove network behavior.

content-navigation.intent: Demonstrate the documentation shell, sidebar, table of contents, breadcrumbs, pagination, and responsive navigation.
intentional_traits: Active routes and sections may be forced for evidence.
Mobile navigation panels may remain open during capture.
The content is deterministic documentation copy.
invariants: Current route, section, and navigation hierarchy must be unambiguous.
Panels must remain within the viewport without hiding essential actions.
Reading measure, shell columns, and scrolling regions must remain coherent.
Keyboard focus indicators must be visible when declared.
exclusions: An open mobile panel is intentional.
Forced active states do not imply broken routing.
The capture does not require real scroll synchronization.

destination-policy.intent: Present allow, confirm, and deny destination policies as explicit host-controlled decisions.
intentional_traits: Several policy outcomes deliberately appear side by side.
Destinations and reasons are deterministic fixtures.
Actions express intentions and perform no navigation.
invariants: Destination, justification, and associated action must remain readable.
Allow, confirm, and deny must be distinguishable without color alone.
Unsafe schemes must never appear equivalent to allowed destinations.
Cards must retain coherent geometry at declared viewports.
exclusions: Showing incompatible policy outcomes together is intentional.
Inactive actions are not broken links.
Fixture URLs are not real navigation targets.

document-loading.intent: Demonstrate document loading, stale-request rejection, cached content, empty results, and explicit errors.
intentional_traits: Asynchronous states are frozen as deterministic fixtures.
Several loading outcomes may appear together.
No real filesystem or network access occurs.
invariants: Loading, stale, ready, empty, and error states must remain distinct.
Status, content, and recovery actions must preserve hierarchy.
Long paths and identifiers must not break layout.
State geometry must remain stable during transitions.
exclusions: Frozen loading does not imply a stalled application.
Simultaneous outcomes are intentional.
The fixture does not prove actual I/O.

interactions.intent: Demonstrate controlled focus, keyboard navigation, selection, resizing, and interaction states.
intentional_traits: Focus and pressed states may be forced for capture.
Multiple controllers may appear on one board.
Reduced-motion scenarios suppress nonessential animation.
invariants: Focused, selected, pressed, and disabled states must remain distinct.
Focus indicators must be visible, contained, and geometrically consistent.
Resize handles and interactive targets must remain discoverable.
No state may cause overlap, clipping, or layout instability.
exclusions: Forced simultaneous states are intentional.
A static capture cannot demonstrate the complete keyboard sequence.
Reduced motion is not missing feedback.
